notes: DCA 6-2015 Table B2, Post Heights Based on Tributary Area for Center Posts (Appendix B, p. B4), transcribed 2026-09-27 (#42 slice B3) from the PDF in the guide's sources, read from the page rendered at 500 dpi in four crops and checked against the text extraction; both agree on all 250 cells. napkin uses it for its middle posts, the centre posts of Figure B1 (p. B1). Rows as in Table B1 (table-b1.json). Notes 1 and 3 sit on the title's 'Based', so apply to every row; note 2 sits on Douglas Fir-Larch, Hem-Fir and SPF, so rides on their groups' rows. Note 4 sits on the Tributary Area heading and is an operation, not a footnote: it is the table's centerPostFactor, 5/4, which napkin applies to a centre post under a continuous beam before the lookup and says so. Not yet reviewed: docs/code-packs/reviews/us-ct-2022/dca6-tableB2.md.

footnotes.text: Assumes No 2. Stress grade and wet service conditions.
Incising assumed for Douglas fir-larch, hem-fir, and spruce-pine-fir.

Some post heights for 4x4 post sizes show a greater load carrying capacity than 6x6 post sizes since different ASTM Standards are used to develop design values for visually graded dimension lumber vs. visually graded timbers.

centerPostFactor.text: Tributary area shall be multiplied by 1.25 at center posts with beams not spliced (continuous).
centerPostFactor.location: Table B2 note 4, p. B4 (its superscript on the Tributary Area heading)
